_comment: Copy to config.json and edit for your booth. Nothing secret belongs in git; secrets go in .env (see .env.example).

build._comment: shapeSizes are the backing bounding boxes in mm; kept modest so prints stay under the 15-min budget. customMax bounds the free-draw shape.
build._outline_comment: Freehand custom-shape healing. outlineCloseMm bridges the gap where the loop didn't quite close; outlineOpenMm deletes spikes/needles thinner than about twice this; outlineSmooth is Chaikin smoothing passes.
build._wall_comment: wallLoops: number of perimeters (Bambu default 2). infillWallOverlap: fraction of a line width the infill reaches into the innermost wall, which prevents a groove at the edges.

speed._comment: mm/min. topSurface is the visible last layer: solid fill turns every line width, and at solidInfill speed the nozzle never reaches the commanded speed before braking for the next turn, so flow varies through every turn. Slower there buys a cleaner top for a few seconds.

calibration._comment: Runs once per print, before the prime line. A full G29 mesh probe costs over a minute — on a 13-minute keychain that is a tenth of the booth's throughput, for every kid. Off means the printer uses the mesh it stored the last time it levelled: level once on arrival from the printer's own screen, or turn bedLevel on for the day's first print. startupMinutes/bedLevelMinutes only feed the time estimate.

colourChange._comment: Inserted at the backing->design transition. M400 U1 is the Bambu A1 pause: it finishes moves and pauses so the operator uses the printer screen's filament menu to unload colour 1 / load colour 2, then Resume.
gcode: M400 U1 ; ===== COLOUR CHANGE: unload colour 1, load colour 2 on the printer screen, then Resume =====

template._comment: Replace start.gcode / end.gcode with the header+footer from a REAL sliced A1 mini file for your filament, so bed levelling / flow calibration run correctly. Placeholders {nozzle} {bed} {nozzleFirst} {bedFirst} are substituted.

output._comment: Where the day's files land. Both accept an absolute path, so they can point at a synced or backup folder while the booth itself runs from local disk — do NOT run the project from inside Google Drive/OneDrive/Dropbox, which sync node_modules and .git file by file and lock them mid-write. e.g. "dir": "G:/My Drive/3DiPad/gcode"

notify._comment: Who sends the WhatsApp: 'ghl' (GoHighLevel inbound webhook — recommended, GHL owns the message + nurture), 'meta' (direct WhatsApp Cloud API, see whatsapp block), or 'none'.

ghl._comment: Inbound-webhook URLs go in .env (GHL_LEAD_WEBHOOK_URL / GHL_READY_WEBHOOK_URL) or here. One URL is fine — branch on payload.event in the GHL workflow.

lan._comment: Bambu LAN-mode auto-send + status monitoring. Turn LAN Mode ON on each printer (Settings > Network) and copy its Access Code + Serial below. Verify with: npm run test-printer
lan._qos_comment: The printer does not acknowledge MQTT publishes, so the start command goes out at QoS 0 and whether it worked is read from the printer's own reported state. startConfirmMs is how long to give it to turn over before saying it never started; maxDispatchAttempts stops a switched-off printer from spinning the whole queue.

fan._comment: Part-cooling fan (0-255). Off on the first layer so it sticks, on for the rest - printing with no cooling causes drooping and stringing.
